Duryodhana, distressed and confused after seeing his brothers defeated in battle, humbly approached Bhishma at night to ask a question.
Duryodhana listed the great warriors on his side and expressed his doubt about why the Pandavas kept winning.
Bhishma advised Duryodhana to make peace with the Pandavas for the welfare of all and the earth.
Bhishma explained that the Pandavas are protected by Vishnu (Krishna) and thus cannot be defeated in battle.
Bhishma recounted a past event where all gods and sages gathered on Mount Mandara, seated around Brahma.
A radiant, marvelous flying chariot appeared in the sky, and Brahma, through meditation, recognized it and paid homage to the Supreme God.
All sages and gods stood up, joined their palms, and witnessed the great miracle.
Brahma, the knower of Brahman and creator of the world, addressed the Supreme God as the wealth, form, lord, and pervader of the universe, identifying him as Vasudeva's son (Krishna).
